questions.question: What is the primary architecture upgrade in React Native's New Architecture over the legacy asynchronous JSON bridge?
options: It compiles JavaScript directly into Swift source code
It replaces the JSON bridge with JSI (JavaScript Interface), TurboModules, and the Fabric C++ rendering engine
It disables all native threads
It eliminates the need for Android SDKs
questions.answer: It replaces the JSON bridge with JSI (JavaScript Interface), TurboModules, and the Fabric C++ rendering engine
questions.explanation: JSI enables direct synchronous C++ invocation between JavaScript and Native runtimes without serialize/deserialize JSON serialization overhead.

questions.question: In iOS development with Swift, what is the default memory management mechanism?
options: Mark-and-Sweep Garbage Collection
Automatic Reference Counting (ARC)
Manual malloc/free
Generational Tracing GC
questions.explanation: Swift uses Automatic Reference Counting (ARC) at compile time to insert retain and release calls, tracking reference counts without runtime GC pauses.

questions.question: In Kotlin / Jetpack Compose, how does the '@Composable' annotation modify a function?
options: It runs the function in a background Coroutine
It transforms the function into an emitted UI node managed by the Compose runtime and recomposition lifecycle
It marks the function as deprecated
It saves function results to SQLite
questions.answer: It transforms the function into an emitted UI node managed by the Compose runtime and recomposition lifecycle
questions.explanation: The Compose compiler plugin transforms @Composable functions into code that registers and updates nodes in the composition tree.

questions.question: What happens when two Swift objects hold 'strong' references to each other?
options: They execute simultaneously in parallel
A retain cycle (memory leak) occurs because reference counts never reach zero
The compiler throws a syntax error
Both objects are immediately deallocated
questions.answer: A retain cycle (memory leak) occurs because reference counts never reach zero
questions.explanation: Strong reference cycles prevent ARC from deallocating memory. Resolving them requires breaking the cycle with 'weak' or 'unowned' references.

questions.question: In Flutter, what is the key distinction between a StatelessWidget and a StatefulWidget?
options: StatelessWidget cannot contain text
StatelessWidget immutable configuration never mutates over time; StatefulWidget maintains a State object across builds
StatefulWidget runs in a separate thread
StatelessWidget can only run on iOS
questions.answer: StatelessWidget immutable configuration never mutates over time; StatefulWidget maintains a State object across builds
questions.explanation: StatelessWidget build functions depend solely on configuration props, while StatefulWidget preserves mutable state via createState().

questions.question: What is the function of the Android 'AndroidManifest.xml' file?
options: To define CSS color themes
To declare app components (Activities, Services), permissions, hardware features, and API requirements to the Android OS
To compile Java bytecode
To store user passwords
questions.answer: To declare app components (Activities, Services), permissions, hardware features, and API requirements to the Android OS
questions.explanation: Every Android app must have an AndroidManifest.xml file at its root describing app structure, components, and requested system permissions.

questions.question: Why is 'FlashList' or optimized virtualized lists preferred over plain ScrollView in React Native for long lists?
options: ScrollView cannot render images
FlashList recycles native views offscreen rather than mounting hundreds of invisible native views in memory
FlashList eliminates JavaScript execution
ScrollView requires internet connectivity
questions.answer: FlashList recycles native views offscreen rather than mounting hundreds of invisible native views in memory
questions.explanation: Mounting hundreds of complex items in a ScrollView exhausts native UI thread memory. View recycling reuses item containers as users scroll.

questions.question: In iOS background execution, what is the BackgroundTasks framework (BGTaskScheduler) designed for?
options: Running continuous 24/7 calculations with no sleep
Scheduling deferred maintenance tasks (database cleanup, ML model training) when the device is locked, charging, and on Wi-Fi
Displaying immediate push banners
Bypassing App Store reviews
questions.answer: Scheduling deferred maintenance tasks (database cleanup, ML model training) when the device is locked, charging, and on Wi-Fi
questions.explanation: Apple limits background execution to preserve battery life. BGTaskScheduler queues tasks that execute during optimal system power windows.

questions.question: In Kotlin Coroutines, what is the difference between 'Dispatchers.Default' and 'Dispatchers.IO'?
options: Default is for CPU-heavy computation (sorting, JSON parsing), while IO is backed by a dynamic thread pool sized for blocking I/O (disk/network)
Default runs on the UI main thread
IO can only make HTTP GET requests
Dispatchers.Default is single-threaded
questions.answer: Default is for CPU-heavy computation (sorting, JSON parsing), while IO is backed by a dynamic thread pool sized for blocking I/O (disk/network)
questions.explanation: Dispatchers.Default caps thread count to available CPU cores for compute workloads, while Dispatchers.IO scales up to 64 threads to tolerate blocking I/O.

questions.question: What is the purpose of Certificate Pinning in mobile network security?
options: Storing API keys in cleartext on disk
Hardcoding the expected server SSL/TLS public key or certificate to prevent Man-in-the-Middle (MitM) attacks by rogue Root CAs
Allowing connections to expired certificates
Compressing network payloads
questions.answer: Hardcoding the expected server SSL/TLS public key or certificate to prevent Man-in-the-Middle (MitM) attacks by rogue Root CAs
questions.explanation: Certificate/Public Key pinning ensures the client only trusts predetermined server certificates, thwarting proxy interception even if a CA is compromised.
